The explicit source formula gives \(ho_{d+1}-ho_d=n-1+1/n-(d+1)>0\) throughout the allowed range. The \(n\) nearest directed-neighbor inequalities telescope, proving the global inradius upper bound; equality forces all center coordinates equal and hence zero. Polar vertex norms are \(\sqrt2/ho_d\). The outer \(n\) neighbor vertices sum to zero, so the average squared distance to any translated center is \(R^2+\|y\|^2\), proving the origin is the unique minimum-enclosing center.

value.rationale: The clock quasi-metric is the explicit canonical construction by which the source realizes the dual cyclohedron as a Kantorovich--Rubinstein polytope. The result gives a complete Euclidean metric profile of all \(n(n-1)\) source facets and vertices, not a single low-dimensional computation: they split into \(n-1\) strict clock-distance shells with exact multiplicity. It identifies unique extremal centers and exact contact sets on both sides of the polar pair, connecting directed transport cost directly to Euclidean convex geometry. The standard nestohedral cyclohedron has different Euclidean geometry, so these formulas distinguish a natural optimal-transport realization rather than merely rephrasing cyclohedron combinatorics.
